lessons.title: Reporting an event
objectives: Tell a coherent story about a familiar community event.
Develop a connected response in a discussion about reporting an event with a reason and relevant detail.

content_sections.title: Notice the connected language (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Read this model: 'I have considered reporting an event, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.' Identify the main point, the linking expression, and the supporting detail. Then explain how the wording helps the speaker achieve this objective: Tell a coherent story about a familiar community event.

content_sections.title: Guided exchange (10 minutes)
content_sections.body: Work with a partner in a discussion about reporting an event. Give a clear main point, support it with a specific reason, and respond to one follow-up question. Use tactful language when the other speaker presents a different perspective.

content_sections.title: Independent connected response (8 minutes)
content_sections.body: Prepare a one-minute response about reporting an event. Organize it into thought groups, stress the words that carry your main point, and finish with a concise conclusion rather than a list of isolated sentences.

exercises.prompt: Choose the most connected and tactful response for a discussion about reporting an event.
options: I have considered reporting an event, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
Reporting an event is a topic, but I will not explain my view.
Several details exist about reporting an event, perhaps.
exercises.correct_answer: I have considered reporting an event, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.

exercises.prompt: Complete this response about reporting an event: 'My experience supports this view ____.'
acceptable_answers: because it offers evidence about reporting an event

exercises.prompt: Read the short response about reporting an event and identify how the writer handles another view.
exercises.stimulus: Although another person may disagree about reporting an event, I can respond politely and explain my reason.

questions.question: How does the writer respond to disagreement?
acceptable_answers: The writer responds politely and gives a reason in the discussion of reporting an event.

exercises.prompt: Speak for 60–90 seconds in a discussion about reporting an event. State your point, support it, and answer one follow-up question.

criteria: Presents a connected main point about reporting an event with relevant support.
Responds clearly and tactfully to a follow-up question about reporting an event.

listening.instruction: Listen once to a short response about reporting an event. Identify the view and supporting reason before the transcript is revealed, then listen again to check the linking language.
listening.goal: Follow the main point and support in spoken language about reporting an event.
listening.transcript: I have considered reporting an event, and my experience shows one useful reason for this view.
listening.question: What view and supporting reason does the speaker communicate?
listening.answer: The speaker connects a considered view about reporting an event to a useful reason from experience.
constraints: Keep the transcript private before the learner answers the first question.
Use only the supplied transcript; do not require media.

speaking.instruction: Roleplay a discussion about reporting an event. Learner role: present and support a view. Tutor role: ask one probing question and offer a different perspective. End after the learner responds tactfully and summarizes the point.
speaking.goal: Sustain a connected, tactful exchange about reporting an event.
constraints: State both roles before beginning the exchange.
Use at most four tutor turns and stop after the learner summary.

pronunciation.instruction: Record the model about reporting an event in meaningful thought groups. Stress the main point and reason, then compare a second attempt with the first for clarity and rhythm.
pronunciation.goal: Make connected speech about reporting an event easy to follow.
pronunciation.target: Thought groups and information stress for reporting an event
constraints: Assess pronunciation only when learner audio is supplied.
Return NOT_ASSESSED when learner audio is unavailable.

writing.instruction: Write 90–120 words about reporting an event. State a position or experience, support it with a reason and example, and acknowledge another perspective. Submit your own draft before asking for feedback.
writing.goal: Produce a connected written response about reporting an event.
constraints: Wait for the learner draft before giving feedback.
Give concise feedback only; do not replace the learner draft.
